prompt_text: What is the difference between RAM and storage in a computer?
output_text: RAM (Random Access Memory) is fast, short-term memory that holds data the computer is actively processing. It is volatile and loses its contents when power is removed. Storage, such as a solid-state drive or hard disk, holds data persistently and retains it when the computer is off. RAM is significantly faster than storage but holds much less data. When you open an application, its data moves from storage into RAM so the processor can access it quickly. The specific performance difference varies by hardware generation.
